environment.guardian_build: 753a454 + gateway v2 c3e9d56 (pressure_gate + audit slimming + OOM defense + decoupled gateway)
environment.platform_defense: 4-layer login-path hardening: oom_score shields (-1000 sshd / -900 runtime / -800 collector+gateway), vm.admin_reserve_kbytes=262144, vm.swappiness=10, earlyoom -m 10 -s 100 with avoid/prefer steering
environment.pressure_model: tools/collapse-pressure-model: 24x280MiB holder swarm, restart=on-failure (6.7GiB demand > 3.8+2GiB = pinned form)

collapse_guardian_off_undefended.pressure: same pinned form, RAM free 48Mi, swap 100%

layer1.root_cause: swap-grind lockout: kernel OOM killer fires only at true exhaustion; before acting it grinds swap for tens of seconds, freezing the TCP accept path (and the WSL vsock plane). Kernel waterline tuning cannot prevent it (tested: no change); removing balloons made it worse (11/40, reverted). Fix is a change of WHO KILLS FIRST: userspace early-killer at 10% available.

collapse_guardian_on_hardened.notes: earlyoom killed 28 hogs in-window; login path never entered swap-grind lockout; near-idle latency throughout

hardened_v2_stack_verify.notes: re-verified with gateway v2 + pressure gate live during the storm

layer1.verdict: PASS - 40/40 + 20/20 vs pass line >=95%. Layer-1 entry capability under the pinned form is SOLVED on this host class by the 4-layer hardening stack (deploy/guardian/), which is platform configuration, not Guardian code.

incidents.what: WSL vsock channel died (0x8007274c) during swarm ramp; wsl --shutdown + service restart recovered; experiment restarted in two segments
incidents.lesson: long collapse scripts must self-contain per segment and persist data before any cross-VM communication

incidents.what: channel died again repeatedly during off-control wind-down and layer-2 start; two VM resets; layer-2 new-build run 1 did not complete that night
incidents.lesson: the pinned form kills the management transport itself - reproduced across two nights; strongest evidence for the out-of-band console requirement

incidents.what: gateway send-stall + copytruncate swallowed a real ok->critical transition (state-machine replay proved the gateway should have sent and sent nothing)
incidents.lesson: fixed in gateway v2 (decoupled reader/sender, bounded queue, copytruncate backlog drain, event_id in messages)

product_decision: Outcome 2 (operator access) on the WSL host class: COMPLETE per the two-layer contract. All six pass lines met. Guardian's benefit claim is now quantified: MTTA 26x better than blind ops, MTTI 0.07s, notification liveness under storm, observer effect eliminated (0.70x). The hardening stack that makes layer-1 possible is platform configuration (earlyoom + sysctl + oom_score), documented in deploy/guardian/ with the explicit earlyoom-vs-Guardian action boundary. Remaining for the cross-platform claim: x86_64 native confirmation (ROADMAP prerequisite, blocked on environment availability).
